name: KVITLECH
description: Kvitlech (Yiddish for 'Little Notes') is a unique Jewish card game developed in the late 18th century, primarily played by Ashkenazi Jews during the festival of Hanukkah. It is a variant of Blackjack or 21, but played with a specialized 'Kosher' deck that lacks standard suits and Christian-influenced imagery. Instead, the deck consists of 24 to 31 cards featuring simple numbers or Hebrew identifiers.

content.text: Kvitlech (Yiddish for 'Little Notes') is a unique Jewish card game developed in the late 18th century, primarily played by Ashkenazi Jews during the festival of Hanukkah. It is a variant of Blackjack or 21, but played with a specialized 'Kosher' deck that lacks standard suits and Christian-influenced imagery. Instead, the deck consists of 24 to 31 cards featuring simple numbers or Hebrew identifiers.

Developed by Hassidic and Orthodox Jews in Galicia to bypass the use of 'standard' cards, which were seen as potentially idolatrous or too secular. Hanukkah was the only time card-playing was culturally permitted in many strict communities.
A Banker is chosen; other players are bettors.
Standard 24-card deck contains two sets of numbers 1-12. No suits, Kings, or Queens.
